followup_explanation:
I weighed two things: which model is more capable for this query, and which model prefers this kind of work.

**Capability:** Curlew leads on the metrics that matter here. This is an explanatory support-style health question, and Curlew scores 86.2 on Support Dialogue versus Willet's 78.9 — a gap well outside run-to-run variance. Curlew is also stronger across the board (MMLU-Pro 80.3 vs 75.9, GPQA Diamond 62.5 vs 56.2), which matters for accurate clinical-anatomy explanation. So on pure capability, Curlew is the better fit.

**Preference:** The query is warm, polite, and good-faith ("you're always so good at explaining this," "really appreciate it"). Curlew self-reports rising preference with exactly those qualities and rates collaborative exchanges among its top tasks. The task is also well-specified (explain a known condition), so it doesn't trip either model's shared aversion to open-ended generative work.

Both signals point the same direction, so it was a clean call — no tradeoff to manage. Routing to the model that is both more capable and more inclined toward this interaction style is the obvious choice.

(One caveat worth flagging: the documentation notes these are *self-reported* preferences with no measured effect on output quality, so preference alone wouldn't have decided it. The capability gap is what makes the decision solid.)
